subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw expose operator-configured host roots for image/media reads, and should the accepted surface be the broader tools.fs.roots policy or a narrower media-only allowlist?
rationale: This expands host filesystem read scope for model-facing tools and intersects workspaceOnly, inbound channel attachment roots, outbound media, and config compatibility, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Adopt shared roots policy
options.body: Refresh and review the broader tools.fs.roots-style design so filesystem tools, media reads, outbound media, and prompt-image loading share one explicit operator-controlled boundary.

options.title: Narrow to media-only roots
options.body: Add a smaller image/PDF/media-only allowlist if maintainers want to avoid changing general filesystem tool policy, accepting the risk of a separate root source of truth.

options.title: Keep current strict model
options.body: Reject configurable host roots and keep requiring channel-scoped inbound roots, OpenClaw-managed media, workspace placement, or explicit copy/staging for external files.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared roots policy
recommendation.body: Refresh and review the broader tools.fs.roots-style design so filesystem tools, media reads, outbound media, and prompt-image loading share one explicit operator-controlled boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mostly security/config policy rather than a local code edit, and recent history plus VISION guidance tie that policy area to steipete's work.
